gen-gf-wallpoet-manrope: Commanding Wallpoet lets daylight slip between its high-rising letters, while Manrope keeps its curves bright and open. Loud above, friendly below; the sans never fights back.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One leaves wide gaps between letters, with hardly any capital step. Grandstander keeps the headline bold and plain, and a long run of that open sans text would drift by smoothly.
gen-flavors-gf-lexend-peta: Whimsical Flavors gives diagonals the same heft as its stems, with a stubby, towering lowercase. And Lexend Peta backs it up with curves that never thin out, for a sturdy, weighty finish.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-montserrat-altern: Grandstander draws plain constant-width lines and keeps its letters held open, never curled shut. Montserrat Alternates brings a c as open as a bent paperclip and lowercase crowding toward the capital line.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-lexend-mega: Instantly distinctive: Gugi cuts its terminals open so counters flow outward, while Lexend Mega draws as if with one nib. Body text comes across modern and friendly, never fussy.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-kadwa: Modern New Title locks its letters together like links in a fine chain. But Kadwa does the quieter work, its open-ended curves and larger-than-usual x-height lending classic editorial weight.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-merriweather: Merriweather Sans makes words look sturdy and large, with an e whose eye opens clearly to the right. Early GameBoy handles the playful shouting; the sans handles the reading.
gen-gf-metamorphous-gf-julius-sans-one: Metamorphous leaves generous room around every letter, with a high-set midline. Julius Sans One, the sans-serif beneath, has no hairlines to squint at, so the two sit comfortably together.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-fs-merriweat: Merriweather Sans is the sturdy, large-looking sans-serif here, with an e that opens clearly to the right. And Eight Bit Dragon, striding across widely separated letters, supplies the adventure.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Raw and chaotic, Disorder sets big lowercase glyphs well apart with no swelling where curves meet stems. But Be Vietnam Pro, with strokes like a bent steel rod, steadies it without dulling the edge.
